_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform. The ✳️any subset registers `lopdf` under `pdf-1-7-mutate` for the DOCUMENT vocabulary; this file registers the same package under a distinct id and the `pdf-1-7-a-mutate` capability the CONFORMANCE-CLASS case (`mutate-pdf-1-7-a`) tags, because reusing a neighbour's entry fails the contract with `oracle-capability-mismatch`.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED, on the same ground as `gltf`, `png`, `jpg`, `bmp`, `tiff` and `avi`. `lopdf` is a real PDF codec and does real work — but what a MUTATION SHOULD PRODUCE is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs`, whose doc comments say it plainly: the forward and undo results are "read out of the BYTES by the INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION". The fixtures registered alongside are generated through that same second implementation (`apply_conformance_mutation` in `semio-s-plugin-stdio-test-oracle`), so both halves of the comparison descend from one reading of the specification, and a misreading of it yields two agreeing wrong answers.

`lopdf` discharges "the result is a well-formed PDF", NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for. A required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute.

The fixtures stay and are valuable: real PDF bytes, byte-reproducible, covering every declared kind of this conformance profile — exactly what a qualifying third-party reference gets pointed at when one exists.

📖️ A READER, over a corpus that had to be REBUILT before one could mean anything.

The previous generator imported `oracle_apply_mutation` and `project_conformance` from `semio-s-plugin-stdio-test-oracle`, this repository's own crate, so the mutated bytes AND the expected projection of them were both ours and `lopdf` was a codec for our own answer. Registering a reader beside that corpus would have changed the label and nothing else.

`🦀️lopdf-engine` depends on `lopdf` and nothing else: it lays out the seed, performs each mutation through lopdf's own public COS API, and reads the conformance axes back through it. It refuses to write a pair whose projection does not move, so a no-op cannot be committed as a fixture that would pass forever.

The two encryption kinds are `-uncarried`, not routed around: lopdf 0.44's writer takes its encryption path whenever the trailer carries `/Encrypt` and then needs the encryption state a genuine decryption would have recorded, so a synthetic encryption dictionary can be neither written nor read back. A writer-side limit, not a reader gap.

📖️ A SECOND reader for the two kinds `lopdf` can neither write nor read.

Both halves were measured. WRITING: lopdf 0.44's writer takes its encryption path whenever the trailer carries `/Encrypt` and then requires the encryption state a genuine decryption would have recorded, so a synthetic encryption dictionary fails on its own output (`object ID 8 0 not found`). READING: handed a genuinely encrypted PDF, lopdf DECRYPTS transparently with the empty user password and then reports `is_encrypted() == false` — so even a real encrypted fixture would project as unencrypted. That is why these two kinds were `-uncarried`, and it was a statement about lopdf, not about PDF libraries.

pypdf 6.14 does both: `PdfWriter.encrypt` emits a real standard security handler, and `PdfReader.is_encrypted` reports it. Its output is byte-DETERMINISTIC — checked three times before it was relied on, which matters because encryption schemes commonly randomise a key and a non-reproducible fixture would fail this repository's own reproducibility gate.

The reader is shared by all four conformance subsets: the question is identical across them and the framework already lets a probe's `command` point at another subset's script.

comparisonProfiles.description: A PDF document compared by the CONFORMANCE-CLASS surface check_pdf_a_conformance actually reads, every field read back out of the bytes by the independent `lopdf` object-graph reader: the page count as a stability anchor, plus every Standard Security Handler dictionary object, by its /V and /R; every /S /JavaScript action, by the script its /JS carries; every /S /Launch action, by the target its /F carries; every /Type /Filespec, by file name, whether it carries an /EF attached stream, and its /AFRelationship; every intent reachable from /Root/OutputIntents, by /S marker, output condition identifier and whether it carries a /DestOutputProfile; every /Type /FontDescriptor in object-number order, by which of /FontFile, /FontFile2 or /FontFile3 carries its embedded program, how many bytes that program is once its stream filters are DECODED, and a digest of those decoded bytes. Page CONTENT is deliberately absent — media boxes, content streams and shown text belong to the ✳️any subset's own semantic-pdf-v1 profile, and a conformance class says nothing about them. Object NUMBERS are deliberately absent too: a class is defined on what the document contains, not on where a writer put it, so re-inserting a removed construct at a fresh number is a faithful undo and recording the number would report a false divergence for it. An embedded font program is measured DECODED and never by the length of the stream that stores it: /FontFile, /FontFile2 and /FontFile3 streams are almost always /FlateDecode, and deflate output length is ENCODER FREEDOM — two conformant writers may compress a byte-identical program to byte counts that differ by a byte or two, which is precisely what the first full differential run of these six classes measured (all 23 embedded programs of the real thesis decoded byte-identically while five of their stored streams differed by 1–2 bytes). The ✳️any subset's semantic-pdf-v1 profile already takes that reading, listing streamLength as writer freedom. Decoding is not a relaxation: the decoded length plus a digest of the decoded bytes is a STRICTER axis than the stored length ever was, because a program whose bytes change is now caught even when its length does not. The only numeric fields are the encryption /V and /R, an embedded font program's decoded byte length and the page-box coordinates, all of them exact integers or literal coordinates a writer must reproduce exactly; hence no tolerance.
Whether the document carries a standard security handler, the handler's algorithm, and the page count read after decrypting with the empty user password so both sides of a pair stay comparable.

Observability was checked through the pypdf reader before the pair was written.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways for all 12 witnessable kinds, per-fixture: (base,base) -> equal:true for 12/12; (base,mutated) -> equal:false for 12/12 — 24/24 directions correct. Observability is also enforced at GENERATION time: the engine refuses to write a pair whose projection does not move. The two encryption kinds were caught by exactly that check failing to read its own output (`object ID 8 0 not found`) and are registered -uncarried.

criteria.detail: 12/12 kinds: identical (base,base) compares equal:true
12/12 kinds: the kind's own (base,mutated) compares equal:false
The reader projects and compares; it neither applies a mutation nor computes an expected state
The corpus regenerates byte-identically; no wall-clock and no randomness in the seed
lopdf 0.44.0 is vendored in the cargo registry cache; builds and runs with --offline
